title: WAMR WASI poll_oneoff output buffer overflow
ai_system: Claude; Anthropic CVD snapshot identifies Claude Mythos Preview; the project advisory says Anthropic ran Claude Code, so the specific model/tool attribution differs by source.
summary: WAMR’s WASI poll_oneoff path fails to validate the output buffer for all events that may be written. A guest module can cause the host runtime to write an event past the allocated buffer, crossing the Wasm linear-memory boundary into adjacent host heap memory. The Anthropic CVD snapshot records repeatable ASan overflow findings; the project advisory and later release material identify the issue and fix. The attack requires execution of a malicious Wasm module in a WAMR host. Do not infer arbitrary code execution from the documented memory corruption.
ai_role: Anthropic CVD item explicitly attributes discovery to Claude Mythos Preview; WAMR’s advisory is the matching issue-level record.
classification_note: Project advisory GHSA-wj3p-xhqm-pffc was published Jul 16, 2026; Anthropic snapshot states public reveal on Aug 17, 2026. This date disagreement is retained here rather than resolved by using a later dashboard update date. WAMR 2.4.5 release notes identify CVE-2026-54914 and fix the poll_oneoff overflow. No exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: WAMR 2.4.5 release notes state that it fixes CVE-2026-54914. The Anthropic CVD snapshot includes the upstream bounds-check change and regression coverage. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A crafted guest module can cause wasi_poll_oneoff to write past validated Wasm linear memory into adjacent host heap; the overwrite can reliably crash the host. Further confidentiality or integrity consequences depend on heap layout and are not asserted as guaranteed.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.
